body:
Hmm..

``` php
User::findOne(['AND', ['email'=>2], [new \yii\db\Expression('username IS NOT NULL')]]);
```

``` sql
SELECT * FROM `user` WHERE `id` IN ('AND', NULL, NULL)
```

Согласно гайду, если не указать массив (ключ-значение), то да - будет поиск по ID, но **у меня массив**.

И там не `['email'=>[2, 'auth_key']],` а `['email'=>2, 'auth_key']`,
и ['and', 'a' => 'A', 'b' => 'B'] не работает,  - https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/issues/7888#issuecomment-86646980, ой там 

``` php
User::findOne(['AND', ['email'=>2], [new \yii\db\Expression('username IS NOT NULL')]]);
```

Но даже, если правильно

``` php
User::findOne(['AND', ['email'=>2], new Expression('username IS NOT NULL')]
```

то возвращается:

``` sql
SELECT * FROM `user` WHERE `id` IN ('AND', NULL, username IS NOT NULL)
```

для 

``` php
find()->where((['AND', ['email'=>2], new Expression('username IS NOT NULL')])
```

работает как надо:

``` sql
SELECT * FROM `user` WHERE (`email`=2) AND (username IS NOT NULL)
```

After all, this code should be executed the same. Am I right?
http://www.yiiframework.com/doc-2.0/yii-db-baseactiverecord.html#findOne()-detail

``` php
User::findOne(['AND', ['email'=>2], new Expression('username IS NOT NULL')]);
User::find()->where(['AND', ['email'=>2], new Expression('username IS NOT NULL')])->one();
```

``` sql
SELECT * FROM `user` WHERE `id` IN ('AND', NULL, username IS NOT NULL) //findOne
SELECT * FROM `user` WHERE (`email`=2) AND (username IS NOT NULL) //find->one()
```

> User::find()->where(['email'=>2, 'auth_key'])->one()

this syntax looks completely wrong, where do you get that from?

> User::findOne(['email'=>2, new \yii\db\Expression('username IS NOT NULL')

this is not valid syntax, you can either use associative array OR compose where with operators. Not both in one array.

However the example in your last comment looks like a bug.

`User::findOne(['email'=>2, 'auth_key'])` is because the array is not a full associative array. So it is considered to be an array of values that the primary key should be in. Note that `findOne()` is not the same as `find()->where()`.

issue.title: ActiveRecord::findByCondition $condition explanation in comments

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
Hello.

I wanted to look into `ActiveRecord::findAll`'s  `$condition` parameter to find out what options it has and kinda failed.

I jumped into the source of `BaseActiveRecord`:

``` php
/**
 * @inheritdoc
 * @return static[] an array of ActiveRecord instances, or an empty array if nothing matches.
 */
public static function findAll($condition)
{
    return static::findByCondition($condition)->all();
}
```

Okay, It's calling `findByCondition`:

``` php
/**
 * @param mixed $condition please refer to [[findOne()]] for the explanation of this parameter
```

But `findOne` doesn't say anything:

``` php
/**
 * @inheritdoc
 * @return static ActiveRecord instance matching the condition, or `null` if nothing matches.
 */
public static function findOne($condition)
```

Hope my explanations are clear. Thanks.

issue.title: ActiveRecord::findAll() and ActiveRecord::findOne() works wrong in some cases

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
``` php
Model::findOne([
    'some' => 1,
    'some' => 2,
]);
```

works

``` php
Model::findOne([
    'and',
    ['some' => 1],
    ['some' => 2],
]);
```

do not works as expected while

``` php
Model::deleteAll([
    'and',
    ['some' => 1],
    ['some' => 2],
]);
```

works as expected

Same things for `findAll`. We have serious inconsistency which lead to bugs and long investigations in 2nd cases. For now workaround is to use `findOne/findAll` with hash format conditions only. If fix was impossible by BC reasons such restrictions should be documented in corresponding methods phpDoc.

issue.title: ActiveRecord findOne ambiguity

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
### What steps will reproduce the problem?
User::findOne(['or', ["email" => $this->username], ["username" => $this->username]])

### What is the expected result?
the actual SQL is  "SELECT * FROM `user` WHERE `id` IN ('or', NULL, NULL)"

### What do you get instead?
But what i want is:
User::find()->where(['or', ["email" => $this->username], ["username" => $this->username]])->one();


### Additional info

| Q                | A
| ---------------- | ---
| Yii version      | 2.0.9
| PHP version      |  5.6
| Operating system | Unbunt 16.04
